title_zh: 你醒了吗-国际安徒生奖
title_en: Are You Awake? - Hans Christian Andersen Award
source_file: 你醒了吗-国际安徒生奖（7-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 你醒了吗
[瑞士] 汉娜·约翰森 文
[德] 罗特劳特·苏珊娜·贝尔纳 图 任庆莉 译

手机淘宝扫一扫

后浪

北京联合出版公司
Beijing United Publishing Co.,Ltd.
1/16

[P3] 当多多醒来时，
如果是冬天，天是暗的；但如果是夏天，天已经亮了；
在春季和秋季，天是半明半暗的。
多多躺在床上。

醒来以后，首先是听到响声。
睡房里面有水声？
浴缸里面有盘子？
厨房的门发出了响声？

她睡不着了，但也没完全醒。
她不知道，外面天是亮了，还是没亮。
她不知道，她还躺在床上。她也不知道，她已经醒了。
她甚至不知道自己是多多。
她真的不知道，她已经不知道自己就是多多。

不对！多多立刻明白，
应该是：
浴缸里有水，
厨房里有盘子，
睡房的门有时会发出轻微的响声。

[P4] 屋顶上停着一架飞机？天上有辆车？
否则会是怎样的呢？有一只鸟在大街上？
要么这样，要么那样。但是，只有当多多又睡着了才行。

[P5] 否则，正常的应该是这样的：
站在屋顶上的是鸟，天上飞的是飞机，大街上跑的是汽车。
当多多明白这些时，她也知道了自己就是多多。

至少她很快就知道了，大多数时候是在此之前。
她当然也明白，她还躺在床上，她醒了。
她唯一不明白的是，她现在该干嘛？
还是先听一听吧。
但也有一些天，什么也听不到，多多这么想。
什么也听不到。其实不是这样的。
总能听到一点什么。
这就要看，是不是真想要听。
多多躺在床上，她早就知道，自己已经醒了，
她在等待，最终总能听到什么。
至少屋顶上有只鸟。什么也没有，还是有一只鸟？

整个房子里一片寂静。没有水声，没有盘子声，没有睡房门的声音。
鱼缸里有轻微的潺潺水声，这没什么特别的。
鱼缸里的水声总是很轻的。
现在该干嘛呢？
如果睁开眼睛会怎样呢？总能看到什么吧。
光线总是透过窗帘的缝隙照进屋里，是那种一道道的光线。
不对，并不是每天如此，只有在有阳光的时候才有一道道的光线。
在冬天，多多醒来时，天是暗的，那就没有亮光进来，
就更谈不上一道道的光线了。但是，现在不是冬天。

多多躺在床上，睁开眼睛，最先看到的，是鱼缸。
上面披了一道道的光线。

[P6] 多多来到过道。
当然是踮着脚尖，轻手轻脚地。
她靠在睡房的门上仔细听，什么也没听见。
既没有咯吱咯吱的床板声，也没有呼呼的鼾声。
他们也许已经醒了，多多想。
多多比其他任何人都擅长悄然无声地开门，
只要推开一点就行。
别的人都不得不停下来，否则门就会发出响声。
多多恰恰知道，门开到什么程度会发出响声。
她站在门缝边。
她听到了呼吸声。
是爸爸和妈妈的呼吸声，非常均匀，
可以听出两人的不同。
多多屏住呼吸。
现在的问题是：她该从哪个人开始？
多多轻手轻脚地来到妈妈睡觉的这一边，
是踮着脚尖走过来的。
她盯着妈妈看了一会儿，看她是如何呼吸的。
“你还在睡吗？”多多尽量轻声地问。
“嗯。”妈妈轻声地回答。
“可惜啊。”多多说。
“是可惜啊。”妈妈说。
现在该怎么办？

[P7] 多多绕过床，
来到爸爸睡觉的这一边，
当然也是踮着脚尖
走过来的。
她盯着爸爸看了一会儿，
看他是如何呼吸的。
“你还在睡吗？”多多尽量轻声地问。
“嗯。”爸爸轻声地回答。
“可惜啊。”多多说。
“是可惜啊。”
爸爸说。

[P8] 多多小心翼翼地下楼，
惟恐楼梯会发出响声。
奶奶住在楼下。
多多轻手轻脚地走过过道，当然还是踮着脚尖。
奶奶的房门没有发出声音。
和多多的房间一样，奶奶的房间也有从窗子射进来的
一道道的阳光。
其实也并不是真的很可惜。
多多从门缝中挤了出去，关上门吗？还是开着吧，免得把妈妈
爸爸吵醒了。多多从来不知道，门会不会在关的时候发出响声。
然后她来到过道，当然还是踮着脚尖。
多多听到了从远处传来的声音，
大街上有一辆汽车，房顶上有一只鸟，天上有一架飞机，
她还听到了奶奶是如何呼吸的。
她是睡着呢，还是醒了？是睡着呢，多多想。

[P9] 我可以问啊！
奶奶不是总说：
问是不会吃亏的。
“你醒了吗？”多多轻声地问。
“是的。”奶奶回答。
“你怎么就醒了呢？”
“我从来不睡啊。”
奶奶轻声说。
“会有这种情况？”
“有的时候。”
奶奶说。
“为什么？”
“我不知道为什么。
你为什么这么问？”
“因为我也愿意这么问。”
“那你呢，你也不睡觉吗？”
“现在不睡。”多多说。

[P10] “那现在不睡的就我们俩啦。”
“不，是我们仨，”多多说，“脚鱼也没睡。”
“现在还早着呢。”奶奶说。
“太好了。”
“为什么太好啦？”
“你可以读书给我听啊。”多多说。
“我该给你读什么呢？”奶奶问。
“当然是一本书！”
“什么样的一本书？”
“就像这本书。”

[P11] 多多给奶奶看了这本书，说，“为什么你会这么问？”
“因为我想这么问啊。”奶奶说，然后她打开书，读了起来，
“多多醒来的时候，如果是冬天，天还是暗的；如果是夏天，
天已经亮了；在春季和秋季，天是半明半暗的。”
“然后呢？”
“多多躺在床上，”奶奶接着往下读，“她睡不着了，但
也没完全醒。她不知道，外面是天亮了，还是没亮。她
不知道，她还躺在床上。她也不知道，她已经醒了。她
甚至不知道自己是多多。她真的不知道，她已经不知道
自己就是多多。”
“还真是这样。”多多说，“接着读。”
“猫不能上床。”
“书上没有这句话！”
多多说。
“你怎么知道的？”
“我就是知道啊。”
奶奶说：“不管书上是否有这句话，事实就是如此。”
“事实是，”多多说，
“那只是指一般的猫。我们的猫不是一般的猫。
再说它已经在床上了。”
猫可以继续待在床上，但只是例外，因为猫真的不能上床。
“接着读。”奶奶接着读，“醒来以后，多多总能听到什么。”
此时此刻，她们听见从楼上传来的声音。
“什么声音？”多多问。
奶奶想了想：“睡房里的水声？浴缸里的盘子声？
厨房门发出的响声？”
“不对。”多多说。
她知道上面发生了什么，她的爸爸妈妈醒了。
“楼上发生了什么吗？为什么他们跑来跑去？”
“不知道。”多多说，
“平时他们不会这样的。”

[P12] 她们听到了下楼梯的脚步声。
突然多多的妈妈站在了屋里，她神情紧张地喊道：
“多多！”，
“你为什么大喊大叫？”，
“我们终于找到她了！”爸爸说。
他也站在了门口。
“你们不要紧张，”奶奶说，
“一切都很正常啊。你们为什么不坐下来？你们也可以听的。”
多多的妈妈笑了，“我们不打搅你们。”她说。
“我该继续读书吗？”奶奶问。
“当然。”

[P13] 奶奶接着读：
“有时候，多多早晨什么也听不到。
大街上没有汽车，房顶上没有鸟，
天上没有飞机。
她能听到的是妈妈的声音。
‘你还在睡吗？’妈妈轻声地问。
‘是的。’多多回答说。
‘可惜啊。’妈妈轻声说。
‘一点都不可惜啊。’
‘为什么不可惜？’
多多说：‘早晨被唤醒也很不错啊，
尤其是到了该醒的时候。’
‘这样啊。’
‘你为什么这么问啊？’多多说。
‘我不知道。’
‘但我知道，你就想这么问。’”

[P14] “你怎么不接着读啦？”多多问奶奶。
“这本书已经读完啦，”奶奶说，
“你为什么这么问？”
full_text_en:
[P1] Are You Awake?
[Switzerland] Hanna Johansen, text
[Germany] Rotraut Susanne Berner, illustrations; Ren Qingli, translator

Scan with Taobao App

Post Wave

Beijing United Publishing Co., Ltd.
1/16

[P3] When Dodo wakes up,
if it's winter, it's dark; but if it's summer, it's already light;
in spring and autumn, it's half-light and half-dark.
Dodo lies in bed.

After waking up, the first thing is to hear sounds.
Is there water in the bedroom?
Are there dishes in the bathtub?
Did the kitchen door make a sound?

She can't sleep, but she's not fully awake.
She doesn't know if it's light outside or not.
She doesn't know she's still in bed. She doesn't know she's already awake.
She doesn't even know she is Dodo.
She truly doesn't know, she doesn't even know she is Dodo.

No! Dodo immediately realizes,
it should be:
There's water in the bathtub,
there are dishes in the kitchen,
the bedroom door sometimes makes a faint sound.

[P4] Is there a plane parked on the roof? Is there a car in the sky?
What would it be like otherwise? Is there a bird on the street?
Either way, or the other. But only when Duoduo falls asleep again.

[P5] Otherwise, the normal should be like this:
Birds stand on rooftops, planes fly in the sky, and cars run on the streets.
When Duoduo understands these, she also knows that she is Duoduo.

At least she quickly realizes that most of the time, it's before this.
She certainly understands that she is still lying in bed, and she is awake.
The only thing she doesn't understand is, what should she do now?
Maybe she should listen first.
But there are some days when she hears nothing, Duoduo thinks.
Hearing nothing? Actually, that's not true.
She always hears something.
It depends on whether she really wants to listen.
Duoduo lies in bed, she already knows she's awake,
she waits, and eventually she always hears something.
At least there's a bird on the roof. Is there nothing, or is there a bird?

The whole house is silent. No water sounds, no clatter of dishes, no sound of the bedroom door.
There's a faint gurgling sound from the fish tank, nothing special.
The water sound in the fish tank is always soft.
What should she do now?
What if she opens her eyes? She should be able to see something.
Light always streams through the gaps in the curtains into the room, in those streaks of light.
No, not every day is like this; only when there's sunlight are there streaks of light.
In winter, when Duoduo wakes up, the sky is dark, so no light comes in,
let alone streaks of light. But now, it's not winter.

Duoduo lies in bed, opens her eyes, and the first thing she sees is the fish tank.
It's covered with streaks of light.

[P6] Duo Duo came to the hallway.
Of course, tiptoeing, quietly and carefully.
She leaned against the bedroom door and listened carefully, but heard nothing.
There was no creaking of the bedboards, nor the sound of snoring.
They might already be awake, Duo Duo thought.
Duo Duo was better than anyone else at opening doors silently.
She only needed to push it open a little.
Others had to stop, or the door would make a noise.
Duo Duo knew exactly how far to open the door before it would creak.
She stood at the crack of the door.
She heard breathing.
It was the breathing of Dad and Mom, very steady,
and she could tell the difference between the two.
Duo Duo held her breath.
The question now was: whom should she start with?
Duo Duo quietly approached the side of the bed where Mom was sleeping,
tiptoeing all the way.
She stared at Mom for a while, watching how she breathed.
"Are you still asleep?" Duo Duo asked as quietly as possible.
"Mmm." Mom answered softly.
"Too bad," Duo Duo said.
"It is too bad," Mom said.
What should she do now?

[P7] Duo Duo went around the bed,
coming to the side where Dad was sleeping,
and of course, she walked on tiptoe.
She stared at Dad for a while,
watching how he breathed.
"Are you still sleeping?" Duo Duo asked as quietly as possible.
"Mm-hmm," Dad replied softly.
"Too bad," Duo Duo said.
"It is too bad," Dad said.

[P8] Duo Duo carefully went downstairs,
afraid the stairs might make a noise.
Grandma lives downstairs.
Duo Duo walked quietly through the hallway, still tiptoeing.
Grandma's door made no sound.
Just like Duo Duo's room, Grandma's room also had rays of sunlight
coming through the window.
Actually, it wasn't really that unfortunate.
Duo Duo squeezed out through the door crack. Should she close the door? Or leave it open, to avoid waking up Mom
and Dad? Duo Duo never knew if the door would make a noise when closing.
Then she arrived at the hallway, still tiptoeing.
Duo Duo heard sounds coming from far away,
a car on the street, a bird on the roof, an airplane in the sky,
she also heard how Grandma was breathing.
Is she asleep, or awake? She must be asleep, Duo Duo thought.

[P9] I can ask!
Grandma always says:
Asking won't hurt.
"Are you awake?" Duoduo asked softly.
"Yes," Grandma replied.
"How did you wake up?"
"I never sleep," Grandma said softly.
"Could that happen?"
"Sometimes," Grandma said.
"Why?"
"I don't know why.
Why are you asking?"
"Because I also want to ask that."
"And you? Are you not sleeping either?"
"Not now," Duoduo said.

[P10] "So now, the two of us are awake."
"No, it's three of us," Dodo said, "the fish aren't asleep either."
"It's still early," Grandma said.
"That's great."
"Why is it great?"
"You can read a book to me," Dodo said.
"What should I read to you?" Grandma asked.
"Of course, a book!"
"What kind of book?"
"Like this book."

[P11] Duo Duo showed the book to Grandma and said, "Why would you ask that?"
"Because I want to ask that," Grandma said, then she opened the book and began reading,
"When Duo Duo wakes up, if it's winter, it's still dark; if it's summer, it's already light; in spring and autumn, it's half-light and half-dark."
"And then?"
"Duo Duo lies in bed," Grandma continued reading, "She can't sleep, but she's not fully awake. She doesn't know if it's light outside or not. She doesn't know she's still lying in bed. She doesn't even know she's awake. She doesn't even know she is Duo Duo. She truly doesn't know, she doesn't know she is Duo Duo."
"That's really true," Duo Duo said, "Continue reading."
"The cat can't get on the bed."
"That sentence isn't in the book!"
Duo Duo said.
"How do you know?"
"I just know."
Grandma said, "Whether the book says it or not, the fact is like this."
"The fact is," Duo Duo said,
"That only refers to ordinary cats. Our cat is not an ordinary cat.
Besides, it's already on the bed."
The cat can stay on the bed, but only as an exception, because cats really can't get on the bed.
"Continue reading," Grandma continued, "After waking up, Duo Duo always hears something."
At this moment, they heard sounds coming from upstairs.
"What sounds?" Duo Duo asked.
Grandma thought for a moment: "Water sounds in the bedroom? Dishes in the bathtub? The noise from the kitchen door?"
"No," Duo Duo said.
She knew what was happening upstairs—her parents had woken up.
"What happened upstairs? Why are they running around?"
"I don't know," Duo Duo said,
"They usually don't do this."

[P12] They heard footsteps coming down the stairs.
Suddenly, Dodo's mother stood in the room, her face tense, shouting:
"Dodo!"
"Why are you shouting so loudly?"
"We finally found her!" said Dad.
He also stood at the doorway.
"Don't worry," Grandma said,
"Everything is perfectly normal. Why don't you sit down? You can listen too."
Dodo's mother smiled, "We won't disturb you," she said.
"Should I continue reading?" Grandma asked.
"Of course."

[P13] Grandma continued reading:
"Sometimes, Dodo can't hear anything in the morning.
There are no cars on the street, no birds on the roof,
no planes in the sky.
All she can hear is her mother's voice.
'Are you still sleeping?' the mother asked softly.
'Yes,' Dodo replied.
'Shame,' the mother said softly.
'Not at all shameful.'
'Why not?'
Dodo said, 'Waking up in the morning is great,
especially when it's time to wake up.'
'Like that.'
'Why do you ask that?' Dodo said.
'I don't know.'
'But I know you just wanted to ask that.'"

[P14] "Why aren't you reading on?" Duoduo asked Grandma.
"This book is finished," Grandma said,
"Why are you asking this?"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页是绘本《你醒了吗》的封面页，展示了书名、作者、插画师、译者信息以及出版社标志，中央有一个太阳和月亮合体的插图。
[P2] 画面描绘了一个宁静的夜晚街景，月亮高悬，一栋房子和一栋砖楼并排而立，屋顶上有猫和卫星天线，窗户透出灯光，街道上有红色小汽车、兔子、青蛙和蜗牛，墙上贴着音乐海报，整体氛围安静而富有生活气息。
[P3] 本页描述了小女孩多多刚醒来时的朦胧状态，她对周围环境和自身身份感到模糊不清，随后通过辨别家中声音逐渐恢复意识。
[P4] 本页描绘了一个充满奇幻色彩的街景，屋顶停着飞机、天上飞着汽车、猫在拉小提琴、鸟在街上行走，文字说明这些奇异景象只有在小女孩多多睡着时才会出现。
[P5] 本页描绘了小女孩多多刚醒来时的内心活动，她通过倾听和观察来确认自己是否真正清醒，思考着周围环境的正常状态，并回忆起自己醒来后最先看到的是鱼缸和透过窗帘的光线。
[P6] 小女孩多多轻手轻脚地来到父母卧室门口，仔细倾听后发现他们仍在熟睡，她屏住呼吸，观察妈妈的呼吸，并轻声询问妈妈是否还在睡，妈妈回答后，多多感叹‘可惜’，并思考接下来该怎么办。
[P7] 小女孩多多轻手轻脚地走到爸爸床边，观察他呼吸并轻声询问是否还在睡，爸爸回答后，多多感叹‘可惜’，爸爸也表示同意。
[P8] 小女孩多多小心翼翼地下楼，轻手轻脚地走过过道，担心发出声音吵醒家人，她观察奶奶的房间并倾听外面的声音，思考奶奶是否还在睡觉。
[P9] 小女孩多多来到奶奶房间，轻声询问奶奶是否醒来，奶奶表示自己从不睡觉，多多对此感到好奇并追问原因，奶奶坦言不知道，多多也表示自己现在不想睡。
[P10] 小女孩多多和奶奶在清晨醒来后对话，多多希望奶奶读书给她听，并指定要读像这本书一样的书。画面展示了家中各成员的状态：父母仍在睡觉，奶奶在厨房，多多在房间看书，猫在跳跃，鱼在鱼缸中游动。
[P11] 多多和奶奶一起阅读关于醒来时感受的书，讨论书中内容与现实的差异，特别是关于猫不能上床的规定。随后，她们听到楼上传来声音，多多判断是爸爸妈妈醒了，并感到疑惑，因为平时他们不会这样跑来跑去。
[P12] 多多的父母下楼后发现她和奶奶在读书，起初紧张，但奶奶安抚他们，邀请他们一起听书，父母表示不打扰并同意继续听。
[P13] 奶奶继续读关于早晨安静的书，描述多多在清晨听不到外界声音，只能听到妈妈的声音。妈妈轻声询问多多是否还在睡，多多表示不觉得可惜，并认为早晨被唤醒很好。多多与妈妈对话，探讨为何妈妈会问这个问题，妈妈表示自己也不知道，但知道多多就是想问。
[P14] 多多问奶奶为什么不继续读书，奶奶回答书已经读完，并反问她为何这么问。画面中，多多、奶奶和父母一起躺在床上，旁边还有一只猫。
